data.revised_prompt:
Edit the provided scientific journal method figure into a cleaner, publication-quality diagram while preserving the original wide aspect ratio, overall left-to-right structure, teal/orange color language, and especially the small pictorial thumbnails inside each module. Keep the figure as a polished vector-like SCI paper diagram on a white background.

Main goal: make the original active-depth mechanism easier to read, not abstract it away.

Layout requirements:
- Preserve the same overall structure and spacing as the input figure.
- Left: keep a visually polished active stereo sensing sketch with a realistic grid wall/target and red projector rays, recognizable as a wall/aperture scene.
- Left lower: a “Geometry stream” section with two map panels labeled exactly:
  - raw depth D_raw
  - scene mask Omega
- Middle-left: a “Camera registers c=[P,E,G]” panel with three vertical controls labeled:
  - P projector power
  - E exposure
  - G gain
- Center: a large teal-framed block titled “S_phi differentiable active-depth sensor”.
- Inside S_phi, keep five horizontal or stacked factor modules with clear pictorial thumbnails, not generic icons:
  1) active return with a range attenuation / laser return visual; label “(P, D_raw)”
  2) ambient washout with a bright noisy/washed surface example; label “(E, Omega)”
  3) motion blur with blurred streaks or a motion example; label “(E, ||v_t||)”
  4) gain / noise with speckled sensor noise texture; label “(G)”
  5) edge difficulty with a depth discontinuity / edge patch; label “(D_raw)”
- Right of S_phi: compact orange/red boxes for:
  - quality Q
  - soft validity M
  - straight-through mask
  - D_obs observed depth
  - Q_obs observed quality

Scientific message and data-flow:
- A native geometric renderer produces raw depth D_raw and scene mask Omega.
- Camera registers c=[P,E,G] control S_phi.
- S_phi models active return, ambient washout, motion blur, gain/noise, and depth-edge difficulty.
- These factors produce a quality map Q and soft validity M.
- A straight-through mask gives observed depth D_obs and observed quality Q_obs.

Formula reduction:
- Remove dense formulas and all long equations from the original.
- Keep only these compact relations, clearly readable:
  - Q = clip(Q0 + Omega C_rho, 0, 1)
  - M = sigmoid(Q)
  - D_obs = D_raw * M_ST
  - Q_obs = Q * M_ST
- Do NOT include long SNR, active signal, passive signal, noise, washout, or edge equations.

Arrows and connections:
- Use only black or dark gray arrows.
- D_raw and Omega feed into S_phi.
- c=[P,E,G] feeds into S_phi and its factor modules.
- speed ||v_t|| may appear as a small fixed context input feeding motion blur only.
- The five factor modules merge into quality Q.
- Q flows to M, and M flows to the straight-through mask, which produces D_obs and Q_obs.

Important constraints:
- Do NOT draw any red dashed gradient/backward lines.
- Do NOT draw any loss box.
- Do NOT imply S_phi outputs x or camera state c.
- Do NOT imply the native renderer R is differentiable in the sensor branch.
- Keep all text large enough to read in a paper.
- Maintain the polished vector-like SCI journal style: white background, teal module frames, orange/red quality/validity boxes, consistent alignment, clean arrows.
- Avoid tiny formulas, dense explanatory prose, watermarks, decorative clutter, misspelled variables.
- Preserve the strong pictorial mini-panels from the original style, but clean them up and simplify formulas throughout.

Make the figure look like a refined redraw/edit of the provided image, not a new unrelated infographic.
